question: 0.4.0: where does a decode step spend its GPU time beyond the weights' bandwidth floor, at one and at eight conversations, and what of it can go without changing a bit of the output?
machine: GMKtec EVO-X2 class, Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (gfx1151), 128 GB, 96 GB carve
model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS, MTP draft head IQ4_XS

profile_method.tool: STRIX_GPU_TIMELINE=N (apply_gpu_timeline_040): a wall_clock64 timestamp kernel captured into the HIP graph after every dispatch, ~0.7-3 us each, subtracted; tables per op class and graph shape
profile_method.why_not_others: STRIX_REPEAT reads a repeated product's weights from the 32 MB cache (a repeated GEMV looks free); the per-node event timer adds ~25 us a dispatch
profile_method.in_run_ab: STRIX_AB=16 (apply_ab_switch_041): the side flips every 16 decode graphs, graphs recaptured, the two graphs after a flip left out. A null A/B (both sides the same code) read +0.3%; sequential runs of the same build read 92.4 / 96.3 / 97.0 ms a step at 8x40K within half an hour
profile_method.summary: tmp/dec040/ab_summary.py <log> [rows]: the per-side medians of the graph spans

one_conversation_profile_3K_0_3_9.small_kernels: ~3 ms of 3-9 us kernels bound by latency, not memory

small_kernels.fused_chains: operands read by kind (direct, linear, scalar), step loop rolled: sigmoid-mul-add 8.4 -> 2.7 us, add-softplus-mul 8.2 -> 2.5, scale-silu 3.5 -> 1.4 (the unrolled general indexing was code fetched at every launch; an unrolled switch made it ~3x slower)
small_kernels.mmvf_few_rows: unroll 4 below 128 rows: the hyper-connection inject 6.0 -> 4.0 us
small_kernels.topk_moe: DPP arg-max, expf not inlined: 10.3 -> 7.8 us (a 10-round serial chain, ~5.5 us warm)
small_kernels.bits: the same arithmetic; STRIX_CHAIN_VERIFY 80 exact / 0 differ

bf16_twins.weights: 264 F32 weights whose every value is a bfloat16 (routers, shared-expert gates, ssm alpha / beta, hyper-connection injects), twins 0.14 GiB
bf16_twins.why_bitwise: mul_mat_vec_f's bf16 loop is its f32 loop and bf16 widens to f32 exactly; GGML_BF16_TWIN_MAGIC keeps a twin on the vector kernel up to 8 columns (bf16 alone takes the WMMA mmf kernel from 4 columns on RDNA3.5, other sums)

records_accumulate.setting: STRIX_GDN_ACC=8 (records a set; 0 or 1: the state written back every short batch as before)

w16_8x2K_step_ms.note: the same gain, deeper replays, twice the record memory

delta_net_state.bits: tmp/dec040/gdn_cols_test.cpp: 78 cases (plain net 1-8 sequences x 1-17 tokens, deferred net with 0-4 records replayed, append with the row kept, replay alone), one column = two columns

ple_drive_wake.finding: tmp/dec041/ssd_latency.cpp on the model file, unbuffered 4 KB reads: back to back 144-153 us; after 1 / 5 / 20 / 80 ms idle 584-648 us; polling the completion instead of waiting 634 us (the drive or its link, not a sleeping core); a wake-up read 500 / 300 / 200 us ahead: 171 / 244 / 332 us
ple_drive_wake.decode_gather: 16 rows a token; with no miss 0.0-0.1 ms, with one miss ~0.7 ms
ple_drive_wake.note: multi_probe's greedy text repeats itself, so one conversation's gathers there never missed; real text misses every few tokens
